newsitem.title: GERMANY: German job deal for foreigners must end fast - Bonn.
newsitem.headline: German job deal for foreigners must end fast - Bonn.

text.p: Contracts signed under a scheme that has brought thousands of workers from eastern Europe to Germany must be allowed to run out as soon as possible, Construction Minister Klaus Toepfer said on Wednesday.

Around 44,000 workers from eastern European countries including Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are employed by German firms under bilateral government agreements. Around half work in the building sector.

Germany has already announced that it will take no more workers under the scheme and Toepfer said in a statement that existing employment contracts, signed between worker and employer, should be wound up as quickly as possible.
"While we fully understand the economic situation of our east European neighbours, the critical state of Germany's own building sector makes this course of action unavoidable," Toepfer said.

Earlier, Germany's Federal Labour Office highlighted the continuing recession in eastern Germany, particularly in the building sector, in figures showing an overall rise in seasonally-adjusted unemployment for July.
German firms have benefited from the scheme because they need only pay the substantially lower employment insurance costs of the guest worker's home country.
They have accused the government of not giving them long enough notice of its intention to ditch the arrangements.
